subject: physics
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: A potential divider consists of two equal resistors across a 9.0 V supply. The output taken across one resistor is:
questions.explain: With equal resistors the supply voltage divides equally, giving 9.0/2 = 4.5 V.

questions.q: Which harmonics are present in a pipe closed at one end?
questions.explain: A closed pipe supports only odd harmonics (1st, 3rd, 5th...) because of the node-antinode boundary conditions.

questions.q: If the speed of an electron is increased, its de Broglie wavelength:
questions.explain: Since λ = h/p and p = mv, increasing speed increases momentum and therefore decreases the wavelength.

questions.q: In the photoelectric effect, increasing the intensity of light above the threshold frequency increases:
options: The number of electrons emitted per second
The maximum kinetic energy of emitted electrons
questions.explain: Higher intensity means more photons per second, so more electrons are emitted, but their maximum KE is unchanged.

questions.q: Why does photoelectric emission occur almost instantaneously when light above the threshold frequency strikes a metal?
options: A single photon delivers all its energy to one electron at once
questions.explain: A photon transfers its energy to a single electron in one interaction, so emission is essentially instantaneous.

questions.q: What distinguishes the EMF of a cell from the terminal potential difference it provides?
options: EMF is always smaller than the terminal pd
They are identical in every circuit
EMF depends only on the external resistance
EMF is energy per coulomb supplied by the cell; terminal pd is the energy per coulomb delivered to the external circuit
questions.explain: EMF is the total energy per coulomb the source provides; terminal pd is what is left for the external circuit after the lost volts across internal resistance.

questions.q: When an electron in an atom moves from a higher to a lower energy level, the atom:
options: Emits a photon of energy equal to the difference between the levels
questions.explain: The electron emits a photon whose energy equals the difference between the two energy levels, hf = E₁ − E₂.

questions.q: Which component allows significant current to flow in only one direction, with a forward 'threshold' voltage of around 0.6 V?
questions.explain: A semiconductor diode conducts only in forward bias above its threshold voltage and blocks reverse current.

questions.q: Two loudspeakers emit sound in phase. At a point where the path difference is 1.5 wavelengths, an observer hears:
questions.explain: A path difference of 1.5λ (an odd number of half-wavelengths) gives destructive interference, a minimum.

questions.q: The de Broglie wavelength of a particle is given by:
questions.explain: The de Broglie wavelength is λ = h/p, where p is the particle's momentum.

questions.q: The photoelectric effect demonstrates that light is:
options: Quantised into discrete packets of energy called photons
questions.explain: The instantaneous, frequency-dependent emission shows light delivers energy in discrete quanta (photons), demonstrating quantisation.

questions.q: How does the resistance of a light-dependent resistor (LDR) change as the light intensity falling on it increases?
questions.explain: Brighter light frees more charge carriers, so the LDR's resistance decreases with increasing illumination.

questions.q: A device operates at 230 V and draws 2.0 A. Its power consumption is:
Two wires are made of the same material and have the same volume. Wire X is twice as long as wire Y. How does the resistance of X compare with that of Y?
questions.explain: Same volume but twice the length means X has half the area, so R ∝ L/A increases by a factor of 2 × 2 = 4.

questions.q: The resistance of a uniform wire is given by R = ρL/A. If the length of the wire is doubled and its cross-sectional area is halved, the resistance becomes:
questions.explain: R ∝ L/A, so doubling L (×2) and halving A (×2) multiplies the resistance by four.

questions.q: The refractive index of a medium is defined as:
options: The speed of light in the medium divided by speed in vacuum
The speed of light in vacuum divided by speed in the medium
questions.explain: Refractive index n = c/v, the ratio of the speed of light in vacuum to its speed in the medium.

questions.q: A 12 V supply is connected across a 6.0 Ω resistor. The power dissipated is:
Which property is unique to transverse waves and cannot occur with longitudinal waves?
questions.explain: Polarisation requires oscillations perpendicular to propagation, so only transverse waves can be polarised.

questions.q: A wave has frequency 50 Hz and travels at 340 m/s. What is its wavelength?
questions.explain: Using v = fλ, λ = 340/50 = 6.8 m.

questions.q: An electron has momentum 3.3 × 10⁻²⁴ kg m/s. Its de Broglie wavelength is (h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s):
The double-slit experiment provided important evidence that light:
options: Behaves as a wave because it produces interference fringes
questions.explain: The interference fringes can only be explained by superposition of waves, supporting the wave nature of light.

questions.q: Kirchhoff's first (current) law is a statement of the conservation of:
questions.explain: The current law (sum of currents into a junction equals sum out) expresses conservation of charge.

questions.q: The photoelectric effect cannot be explained by the wave model of light mainly because the wave model predicts:
options: Instant emission at all frequencies given enough intensity
questions.explain: The wave model predicts any frequency could eventually free electrons with enough intensity/time, contradicting the observed threshold frequency.

questions.q: A line emission spectrum consists of discrete coloured lines because:
options: Atomic electrons occupy only discrete energy levels
questions.explain: Discrete spectral lines arise because electrons occupy quantised energy levels, so only specific photon energies are emitted.

questions.q: Ohm's law states that, for an ohmic conductor at constant temperature:
options: current is proportional to potential difference
current is inversely proportional to potential difference
questions.explain: For an ohmic conductor at constant temperature the current is directly proportional to the pd across it.

questions.q: The ionisation energy of an atom is the energy needed to:
options: Completely remove an electron from the atom in its ground state
Excite an electron to the next level
questions.explain: Ionisation energy is the energy required to remove an electron entirely (to the n = ∞, zero-energy level) from a ground-state atom.

questions.q: A string of length 1.2 m fixed at both ends vibrates in its fundamental (first harmonic) mode. The wavelength is:
questions.explain: The fundamental has one antinode and length = λ/2, so λ = 2 × 1.2 = 2.4 m.

questions.q: As the temperature of an NTC thermistor rises, its resistance:
questions.explain: A negative temperature coefficient (NTC) thermistor releases more charge carriers as it warms, so its resistance falls.

questions.q: An electron drops from an energy level of −1.5 eV to −3.4 eV. The energy of the emitted photon is:
questions.explain: Photon energy = |E_final − E_initial| = |−3.4 − (−1.5)| = 1.9 eV.

questions.q: The maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons depends on:
options: The intensity of the incident light
The frequency of the incident light
The size of the metal plate
questions.explain: Max KE = hf − φ, so it depends on the frequency of the light, not the intensity.
